messages.subject: Compiled nimbleFunction in model
parts:
Hi there!

I have a really short question.

I tried to use my-defined function("solveplus" as example below) in my model.
I wanted to calculate faster, then I tried to use "compiled my-defined function(Csolveplus)"

However, nimbleModel() returned this error message, 
Defining model Error in getSymbolicParentNodesRecurse(code, constNames, indexNames, nimbleFunctionNames, : R function 'Csolveplus' has arguments that cannot be evaluated in the code 'Csolveplus(x, y)'. Either the function must be a nimbleFunction or values for the following inputs must be specified as constants in the model: x,y.

I thought from this error message, I can't use compiled nimbleFunction in my model because the argument of my function must not be constant. It is defined in my model.

How can I use my-defined compiled function with not constant argument?
Or I have to use this function as "uncompiled function"?

Thank you for reading and I'm preasured if you reply me!

Best, 
Oyama



solveplus <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(X = double(0), y = double(0)) { # type declarations
    ans <- X+y
    return(ans)
    returnType(double(0))  # return type declaration
  } )
Csolveplus <- compileNimble(solveplus)

## test example
a = Csolveplus(1, 2)
a # return 3
testcode <- nimbleCode({
  x ~ dnorm(0,1)
  y ~ dnorm(0,1)
  a <- Csolveplus(x, y)
})
test <- nimbleModel(testcode,check = TRUE)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Compiled nimbleFunction in model
parts:
Dear Oyama,
You don't need to change your model code to use a compiled version of solveplus. When you compile the model, it will automatically use a compiled version of solveplus.
HTH
Perry
